fact: Paratus Group (press release republished by ITWeb Africa) says it switched on on 2026-02-09 the 2,000km protected terrestrial G2M fibre route from Goma in eastern DRC via Kigali (Rwanda), Kampala (Uganda) and Nairobi (Kenya) to Mombasa on the coast, now live and carrying traffic, linking DRC to coastal subsea cable capacity.

Paratus says the G2M Goma-Mombasa route is already carrying traffic for its first wholesale customers and is designed for carriers, ISPs and enterprises, i.e. operators other than the owner buy capacity on it.

Airtel Congo RDC SA says it became the first operator in DRC to put the first phase of the 2Africa submarine cable into service, activating an initial 200 Gbps on 2025-12-18; the document names no landing station.

Agence Ecofin, citing TeleGeography's Submarine Cable Map, says two systems land at Moanda, DRC's cable landing: 2Africa (commercial service in DRC with 200 Gbps activated by Airtel on 2025-12-18) and WACS (in service since 2012, serving DRC); both at the same landing point, so two routes, not independent.

Paratus activated a 2,000 km protected fibre route from Mombasa to Goma via Nairobi, Kampala and Kigali, giving eastern DRC direct high-capacity access to subsea systems on the Kenyan coast (route enters DRC from Rwanda); the document attributes this to Paratus.

Paratus says its 2,000 km Goma-to-Mombasa (G2M) terrestrial fibre route from Goma in eastern DRC, through Kigali (Rwanda), Kampala and Nairobi, is live and carrying traffic, giving access to subsea capacity landing at Mombasa.

Connecting Africa says WACS is one of two international submarine cables connecting the DRC to the global internet, the second, 2Africa, having landed in September 2023 and gone live in December 2025.

Ecofin Agency reports that 2Africa (design capacity up to 180 Tb/s, commercial service in the DRC from December 2025 per Airtel) and WACS (in service since 2012) both land at Muanda on the DRC's Atlantic coast.

Agence Ecofin reports that DR Congo depends on two submarine cables, WACS connected in 2013 and 2Africa, which landed in September 2023 and was put in service in December 2025 by Airtel RDC at 200 Gb/s.
